checks.label: Product images have descriptive alt text

checks.label: Canonical points to the source product
checks.detail: Local preview identity only; destination-store canonical and metadata remain an external check.

checks.label: Related collection link is present

checks.label: Product JSON-LD matches local product and price
checks.detail: Local JSON and source-value consistency only. Google Rich Results validation is separate.

checks.label: Search snippet has useful title and description lengths
checks.detail: Local editorial guideline: title 25–70 characters and description 80–165. Presence alone is not useful snippet copy or a ranking guarantee.

checks.label: Substantive product detail beyond name and price
checks.detail: At least two verified product details and 60 words of explanatory copy. Repeating a product name, price or generic selling language is not substantive product information.

checks.label: Useful FAQ answers are actually rendered
checks.detail: At least two real product questions with visible, non-empty answers; add verified product facts when information is missing.

checks.label: Answers are concise and stand alone
checks.detail: Do not replace a useful answer with a source-data disclaimer or a pointer to another paragraph.

checks.label: FAQ markup agrees with visible questions and answers

checks.label: FAQ answers trace to source or merchant facts

checks.label: Answers cover specific buying questions beyond identity and price

researchInfluences.observation: The page uses a large hero banner above the shopping area, with short, centered promotional headline treatment and decorative lifestyle imagery.
researchInfluences.application: I kept a strong opening headline, but moved the hero into a split product layout instead of a category banner and used the product images as the lead visual evidence.

researchInfluences.observation: The product page places a large image beside a purchase panel and includes a second thumbnail angle, with the add-to-cart control directly under the core product info.
researchInfluences.application: I used a right-side media hero with a strong image share, then kept the purchase section close to the bottom after explanatory sections so the page still ends in a clear buying action.

researchInfluences.observation: The page uses question-led educational content blocks and a visible FAQ approach to answer shopper concerns in a more editorial way than a plain product card.
researchInfluences.application: I made the FAQ its own high-contrast section near the end, after the factual and image-led sections, to answer confirmed questions without adding unsupported policy detail.

researchInfluences.observation: The collection page uses wide whitespace, a category-first structure, and a left filter rail that keeps the shopping area open and readable.
researchInfluences.application: I avoided a dense card-grid feel by giving the story and gallery sections more breathing room and using contained width only where the content is truly factual or utility-driven.

researchInfluences.observation: The product page uses a two-column structure with image on one side and price, quantity, and primary add-to-cart directly under the title on the other.
researchInfluences.application: Keep the hero purchase-first and easy to find, but shift to a showcase geometry with the media on the right and three source images so the first screen feels materially different from a simple split page.

researchInfluences.observation: The collection page uses a large banner-led opening with overlaid category messaging and a product grid that follows underneath.
researchInfluences.application: Echo the sense of a strong opening statement, but turn it into a product-specific showcase hero and then move into a full-width story band instead of a grid-led collection structure.

researchInfluences.observation: The page mixes product imagery with question-led educational content and a visible FAQ section below the main shopping area.
researchInfluences.application: Place FAQ after the story and benefits so the page can answer practical questions without interrupting the object-led visual flow.

researchInfluences.observation: Collection cards and supporting content rely on large product imagery and utility-focused shopping cues such as quick shop and clear price presentation.
researchInfluences.application: Use an image-forward treatment with visible purchasing controls in the hero, but avoid repeating a card-grid format by giving later sections wider editorial spacing and different heading placement.

researchInfluences.observation: The product page places the main image on one side and the purchase stack on the other, with price, variant selector, quantity, and add-to-cart kept close together.
researchInfluences.application: I apply that purchase logic in a compact hero stack so buying actions remain immediately visible, but I replace the side-by-side framing with a vertical stack to avoid repeating the same geometry.

researchInfluences.observation: The page uses question-led FAQ headings as a utility section beneath image-led shopping content.
researchInfluences.application: I place the FAQ later in a centered band and keep the questions factual, using that utility-role as a structural anchor rather than a dense text dump.

researchInfluences.observation: The collection page combines a collection title, filtering logic, and a visible FAQ section after the product area, creating a practical editorial-to-utility transition.
researchInfluences.application: I echo that transition by moving from story into a more technical benefit grid and then into an FAQ band, making the page feel progressively more utilitarian.

researchInfluences.observation: A large lifestyle hero with centered category text sits above a restrained product grid, with an editorial tone and minimal supporting copy.
researchInfluences.application: I borrow the restrained editorial tone but keep the product page more focused on the confirmed mug and cart controls, using centered treatment only in the FAQ band rather than in the hero.

researchInfluences.observation: Product page uses a two-column hero with main image left and purchase panel right, plus quantity and add-to-cart directly under the variant area.
researchInfluences.application: I use a rail hero with the image anchored on one side and the buying controls kept in the opposite column so the purchase path is immediately visible.

researchInfluences.observation: The page includes question-led FAQ content and places add-to-cart directly on the shopping path rather than burying it in secondary content.
researchInfluences.application: I place the FAQ after the initial editorial section and keep a dedicated purchase section at the end so shopping remains obvious throughout the page.

researchInfluences.observation: Collection pages use a large hero banner with overlaid title and then move into broad, breathable content spacing.
researchInfluences.application: I increase vertical rhythm with a full-width story section and generous spacing instead of compressing every block into identical cards.

researchInfluences.observation: Collection layouts mix filter-like utility with editorial description and FAQ content, rather than relying on one repetitive module type.
researchInfluences.application: I vary section surfaces and heading placement across story, benefits, FAQ, and purchase so the page feels edited and structurally distinct.

researchInfluences.observation: Two-column product page with large image left and purchase panel right; add-to-cart sits directly under quantity, and the image area includes alternate views.
researchInfluences.application: I mirror the direct purchase logic, but flip the visual emphasis: the hero becomes offset with media on the right and a compact content column, keeping quantity and cart near the top while avoiding a copied left-image/right-buy-panel arrangement.

researchInfluences.observation: Centered category title over a large lifestyle hero with a restrained descriptive paragraph, followed by a clean product grid below.
researchInfluences.application: I borrow the calm editorial pacing and centered heading feel, but use it in a single-product story band rather than a collection grid so the page remains native to one item and not a repeated shop-all layout.

researchInfluences.observation: Collection pages use a promo/utility structure with clear shopping controls, FAQ content below, and a dense product-first hierarchy.
researchInfluences.application: I place a compact purchase section before the FAQ so the shopping action stays easy to find, then end with utility content in a restrained narrow width, translating the research into a cleaner single-product flow.

researchInfluences.observation: Wide collection hero with breadcrumb/title treatment and a separate filtered shopping area beneath; the page uses a strong top banner and then transitions into a more functional shopping zone.
researchInfluences.application: I create a pronounced transition from an image-led hero to a more functional purchase band with a different surface and tighter width, so the page visibly shifts from editorial to transactional instead of repeating one box style.

fingerprint.name: Quiet Object Study
fingerprint.rationale: The source images and description point to a single ceramic mug with warm chestnut glazing and soft-lit neutral presentation, so the strongest direction is a gallery-style product story that gives each image room to feel like an artifact. Because there are multiple source images, the page can move from a large hero image to tighter detail moments without inventing lifestyle context or material facts.
